Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea August 16, 2026 09:45 PM GMT Amazon.com Inc | North America AWS's Path to $1 Trln of Revenue and How AMZN Shares Can Double We detail AWS's road to $1trln of revenue in the next 8-10 years, which paints a path toward $500bn of company-wide EBIT and a $500 share price by year end 2027. Base case remains $335 (~30% upside) with bull case increasingly in play if AWS delivers like we think it could. AMZN's $1 Trillion Vision for AWS Revenue Reinforces the High ROIC Opportunity Ahead: We laid out the high ROIC opportunity for hyperscalers (like AWS) through the GenAI age of inference ahead here, and believe AMZN is confident too given 2Q:26 earnings commentary laying out a vision of $1trln of AWS revenue (~6X larger than the current ~$170bn annualized) with long-term returns similar to the core AWS business over the past ~20 years. AMZN said: “We long believed AWS could become a few hundred billion dollar revenue business and now believe it'll be at least double that, and very possibly be $1 trillion annual revenue business for us in time with very appealing accompanying free cash flow and return on invested capital.” “We've done this before in the first era of cloud computing, just over a longer time horizon where demand built more gradually than it has in AI. But we see the margins and returns in AI tracking what we saw with core at the same point of evolution. Actually a little ahead.” But how far away could AMZN's vision for a trillion dollar business be and what's priced in AMZN shares? Bringing on Compute Capacity Remains the Gating Factor… As long as innovation and demand for GenAI tools continue to scale, we still believe each hyperscaler's ability to bring on compute capacity is the key factor driving forward revenue growth, as explained by our work here. We estimate AMZN is going to bring on 6/8 GW of compute capacity in '26/'27. We acknowledge limited visibility into how many GW of compute AMZN will be bringing online beyond '27 given unknown server/rack purchase volumes, improving server/rack power draws, evolving regulatory unknowns, and physical limits to faster data center openings like labor, construction, and power. But we do believe AMZN is executing at an organized and rapid and clip in order to bring on its current capacity, so as a base case (in this scenario) we assume adding 8 incremental GW per year is a reasonable range going forward.

Source: Company Data, Morgan Stanley Research …While Monetization Rates of Capacity Showcase How $1trln of Revenue Could Be as Soon as 2034: In our GenAI ROIC work, we detailed multiple reasons why implied incremental revenue per incremental GW for the hyperscalers should rise from the current high single digit range to double digit or teens levels. Monetization rates will come down to supply and demand and compute pricing, which is driven by product innovation. AWS is currently monetizing at $8/incremental watt (full year '26 estimate) and we expect this to rise...and consider that if AWS could monetize at $12/incremental watt (on average) it would yield $1trln of revenue as early as 2035. Monetization of $14-$15/incremental watt could bring it even earlier in 2034. Please let us know if interested in our AWS interactive monetization models. Exhibit 2: We see AWS reaching $1trln in revenue as soon as 2034 if monetization rates per incremental GW reach $14-$15...with even $12/ incremental watt yielding $1trln in 2035 And if AI Margins Track with Core Cloud, ~$300bn of AWS EBIT and ~$500bn in Total AMZN EBIT Could Follow: We can debate the long-term margins of a GenAI enabled AWS, but if AMZN management’s comments on AI tracking toward similar margins and returns as core cloud are in the right ballpark, this likely implies ~30% EBIT margins…which means that $1trln of AWS revenue could imply ~$300bn of AWS EBIT in 2034-2036. And as shown below (see Exhibit 4 ), layering in reasonable Retail assumptions, this would imply AMZN is set to generate ~$500bn of EBIT in 2034-2036...and that company wide EBIT could CAGR at a 16-20% rate.
